newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Greens want to swap govt cars for bikes.
newsitem.headline: German Greens want to swap govt cars for bikes.

text.p: If Germany's environmental Greens party gets its way, Chancellor Helmut Kohl and other government leaders may be riding bicycles rather than luxury cars through the government quarter in Berlin.

The party said on Tuesday it planned to urge parliament in car-loving Germany to consider a proposal to swap some of the Mercedes-Benz luxury cars used to chauffeur deputies and government officials around the government quarter for bicycles.
Parliament is due to move to Berlin in 1999.

A spokesman for the Greens said enough money could be saved by giving up just one of the dozens of limousines available for parliamentarians and government leaders for about 50 bicycles and a repair station.

The Greens argue that bicycles would furthermore be better suited for the short distances in the Berlin government quarter, where most buildings and ministries are within one to two kilometres (miles) of each other.

But the Greens, aware of the powerful attachment most deputies have to the cars, are not optimistic that the bid will be any more successful than a similar effort to acquire 50 bikes in Bonn that failed two years ago.
"The chances of seeing Helmut Kohl on a bike in Berlin are very slim," said a Greens spokesman. "Very slim indeed."
